reflection.what_worked: Measuring the blast radius before moving anything surfaced the territory conflict while Phase 1 could still be closed cleanly, and running every downstream phase's read-only probes while blocked meant Phases 2-7 ran without re-measuring. Depth-first phase closure with a commit per phase kept attribution clean against a concurrent dispatch in the same tree.
reflection.what_was_hard: Four separate measurement bugs each made correct work look broken: a piped build exit code masking the guard's, a rename audit whose pathspec named only the destination and so reported a phantom 1313-line rewrite, a sed whose delimiter collided with its own alternation and silently matched nothing, and pgrep/grep patterns matching themselves or a longer prefix. Distinguishing a broken measurement from a broken change was most of the verification effort.
reflection.what_was_missed: The path sweep's pattern assumed a FormalSystem/ prefix and so missed two relative links (../../../PlusLanguage/README.md and its Star counterpart), which only surfaced via readme-lint Check 3. A blunt dotted-path regex also over-applied to two declaration names in the flat namespace. Both argue for letting gate output rather than a pattern decide when a sweep is complete.

memory_candidates.content: A piped build command reports the pipeline's exit status, not the build's: `lake-build-guard.sh ... | tail -30` yields tail's exit code, ~always 0, masking a failed build. Capture the guard's own code un-piped (`cmd > log 2>&1; echo GUARD_EXIT=$?`) or require an explicit 'Build completed successfully (N jobs).' line plus a zero 'error:' count.

When auditing a git mv for content changes, the pathspec must name BOTH the old and new paths, or `git diff -M` cannot pair the rename and every moved file reports as wholly added - looking like a total rewrite. Restricting to the destination alone produced a phantom 1313/1364/1641 changed lines where the true answer was 0/0/0.

A rewrite sweep needs a match-count assertion on both sides, not just a clean exit. A sed using `|` as both the delimiter and the BRE alternation operator (`s|^a\(x\|y\)|...|`) matches nothing and exits 0; the no-op surfaced only because the residual count was unchanged.

Renaming a Lean module path must not rename the namespace: a dotted name in prose may be a namespace/declaration reading (correct as written) or a module-path reading (needs repathing), and the two are textually identical. A blunt regex repathed FormalSystem.StarLanguage.StarAxiom, a declaration, breaking C5 and stranding its allowlist entry. Classify each token against its context first.

When /orchestrate dispatches concurrent implementations with directory-level territories, intersect each plan's per-phase 'Files to modify' list against the assigned territory first. A module-path rename's import-rewrite set routinely reaches outside the directory being renamed, so a territory drawn around that directory alone blocks the task's central phase.

Repairing a dangling documentation link often means correcting a claim, not just a path. Two links to .github/workflows/docs.yml also asserted the workflow 'runs on every push to main', false since it was renamed to .disabled - repathing alone would have turned the gate green while preserving a false statement.
